title: Governments worldwide are way behind on AI, says Bill Gates
key_facts: Bill Gates told Reuters in an interview that 'no government in the world' is ready for the changes AI will bring.
Gates, until recently optimistic, warned about threats to jobs, attacks and addiction to AI companions.
He said 'I don't think any government is nearly as deep on this as they have to be'.
His foundation said on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026) it plans to spend at least $1 billion over two years on expanding access to AI, part of its plan to spend $9 billion a year.
The money goes to partners in education, healthcare and agriculture, and to making large language models work in every language.
He likened AI to an 'alien intelligence' and said countries must cooperate as in disaster movies; he has talked to Trump's team and aims to meet Xi Jinping later this year.
quote_evidence: “I don’t think any government is nearly as deep on this as they have to be,” he said.
“AI is kind of like this alien intelligence. It’s here, and we better do like it shows in those movies.”

The foundation’s $1 billion spending plan, part of its previously announced plans to spend $9 billion annually, will go to partners working in education, healthcare and agriculture, the foundation said.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading philanthropist who has turned more cautious warns that governments are unprepared while his foundation funds access to AI.
event_date: Interview published 9 Oct 2026; foundation announcement Tuesday 6 Oct 2026
notes: Read Interaksyon's Reuters-based text; the page names Reuters as the interviewer. Interview date not stated.
